findings.title: The repair for the 'all external components' coverage limb is circular: both new clauses quantify over components already in the corpus, so neither requires any component to be in it. The single-component false-pass path charged at v1 survives unchanged.
whatWasAdded: A new top-level field, allExternalComponents: 'Every external component in the corpus is in scope. A skipped external component fails. This is not a security-confinement claim.'
A new failsIf entry: 'an external component in the corpus is skipped'.

whyItDoesNotBind.circularity: Both additions are scoped by the phrase 'in the corpus'. They forbid skipping a component that is already in the corpus; neither states which components the corpus must contain. A corpus whose external-component set has exactly one member satisfies both vacuously — that one component is in scope and is not skipped.
whyItDoesNotBind.theGlobalQuantifierIsUnchanged: passProperty is byte-identical to v1 on this point and still quantifies over classes only: 'each retained-evidence member's passProperty holds for every live-cell class, every CC-1..CC-11 class, NT-1, NT-2, NT-6, and FC-NC-CA1-PROCESS-TREE.' No component, role, major or runtime dimension appears in it.
whyItDoesNotBind.noComponentAxisIsEnumerated: namedCorpusWhenFixturesExist enumerates only classes — ten live-cell, eleven CC, three NT, one FC-NC, and four not-executed NT ids. It carries no component axis at all, so nothing else in the artifact supplies what the new field presupposes.
whyItDoesNotBind.noMemberCrossesIt: No exactByteIntent names a per-component, per-role or per-major dimension. Every one of the six is written per class.
whyItDoesNotBind.theSurvivingPath: Exactly the path charged at v1: a corpus exercising all ten live-cell classes, all eleven CC classes, NT-1, NT-2, NT-6 and FC-NC-CA1-PROCESS-TREE against a single external component satisfies every pass property in the file, including allExternalComponents and the new failsIf line, while covering one component out of all external components. The register threshold cell it is meant to bind is unmet and the specification cannot say so.

findings.theAxisExistsInThePinnedSources: The charge does not ask the author to invent a dimension. control-protocol-contract.v2, which this artifact pins at a digest reproduced here, carries 'major' 30 times, 'majors' 4, 'provider major' 5, 'role' 32 and 'runtime' 6, and its CC classes are written against a component under test. provider-only-output-contract.v3, also pinned, carries 'role' 4 times and 'provider' 18. The phrase 'external component' itself occurs zero times in either, and exactly once in file 08 — in this gate's own threshold cell — which is why the artifact has to say what the axis is rather than borrow it.
findings.operativeBite: The register threshold cell for DR-G21 is 'all external components; does not claim security confinement'. The disclaimer limb is honoured thoroughly, in passProperty, failsIf and doesNot. The coverage limb is quoted verbatim into waiverRuleVerbatim and, after this revision, gestured at in two places that cannot fail. Half of a two-limb threshold is bound. At qualification a run could satisfy this specification completely while the gate's stated coverage was not met, and nothing in the artifact would register that.
notRescuedBy: The new failsIf line does not rescue it. It shares the same 'in the corpus' scope as the field, so it fires only on a component already present.
The class enumeration does not rescue it. Classes and components are different axes; exercising every class against one component is what the finding describes.
waiverRuleVerbatim does not rescue it. Quoting the cell is what v1 already did; the charge was that quoting it is not binding it.
findings.remedyShape: Bind the limb rather than restate it. Either enumerate the component axis the corpus must cross — a scope field naming the roles, provider majors or runtimes drawn from the pinned control-protocol-contract.v2 and provider-only-output-contract.v3 — or extend the global passProperty so the class set is quantified over that axis, as the G12 sibling does with modes: ['core','project'] and per-mode members. Either way the failing condition must be a component absent from the corpus, not a component skipped within it. This reviewer enumerates no axis, names no role or major, and writes no scope text.
findings.gradeRationale: Graded SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker for the same reason as at v1: it does not misstate anything, invents nothing, and creates no false claim — it under-specifies one limb of the threshold. Graded SHOULD-FIX and not advisory because the limb is half of the register's stated threshold for this gate, the artifact now contains text that reads as binding it and does not, and a later reader is more likely to believe the limb is covered than they were at v1.

decision.rule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
decision.recommendation: DO-NOT-SEAL. Do not record. Four of the five v1 findings land, two of them blockers, and the repairs are clean and well-sourced; they should be kept verbatim. A v3 that binds the coverage limb — a component axis the corpus must cross, or a global passProperty quantified over that axis, with the failing condition being a component absent from the corpus rather than skipped within it — would, on these bytes, carry no remaining finding known to this reviewer.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: v2 clears both blockers and two of the three SHOULD-FIXes. B1 is repaired by deleting the restart disjunct outright rather than qualifying it: the pass property is now same-live-process, any PID replacement fails, 'A recorded supervised restart is not a pass' is stated, measures is aligned, and a failsIf line was added — which also closes the undecidable-from-the-bytes limb, since PID replacement is exactly what the three retained snapshots can decide. B2 is repaired by listing OBL-G12-HARNESS-SPEC, so one closed plus nine remaining now equals the live D-164 ten-member set exactly, with noteOnG12 rewritten from a substitute into an explanation. SF1 is repaired by removing the header key and replacing it with namesRemaindersOf plus a naming-is-not-execution note. SF2 is repaired by guarding all six exactByteIntent entries with 'Once authored:'. Every mechanical check is clean: subject unmoved at 360c5e2e and 0444, nine of nine cited digests equal live bytes, six member strings ordered-exact against the live DR-G21 evidence cell, claim, waiver, owner and harnessId exact, the ten-item live-cell corpus matching the live harness cell in order, CC-1..CC-11 matching control-protocol-contract.v2 and NT-3/NT-5/NT-4/NT-7 correctly excluded against provider-only-nt-gate-join.v6, file 08 pin equal to live and unmodified, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, prohibition scan clean. One SHOULD-FIX stands: SF3 is not landed. The added allExternalComponents field and its failsIf line both quantify over components 'in the corpus', so they forbid skipping a component already present without requiring any component to be present. The global passProperty is unchanged and still quantifies over classes only, and namedCorpusWhenFixturesExist carries no component axis. The single-component false-pass path charged at v1 therefore survives intact, now behind text that reads as though it had been closed.
